note: Printed claims only (Step 6). No errata touch this program (errataRefs empty); wires = the printed 40 less the free-ended line 6E/free*, which is script cord 39 on 6E#2 (6E#1 holds 5E/6E) with a free end. Nominating the goal moves its free end to D5#2 (D5#1 holds 4L/D5), then, after the printed re-set, to D3#2 (D3#1 holds 3H/D3) and then D7#2 (D7#1 holds 4H/D7); removing the connection returns it to a free end at 6E#2. The goal order D5, D3, D7 is a script choice; each goal runs the printed cycle (explore, nominate, pb6, pb5, pb6, remove the connection, pb4). Asserted: the dial rests on the start position c1 after power on and after each pb5; it rests on the goal position (c5, c3, c7) after the goal pb6 push and after the pb6 push from start. The c3/c5/c7 asserts rest on the panel decimal numbering (DN is dial position N, BK1 printed p.20 = book1.pdf PDF p.22), not on Book V text, which pairs the goal wire with D3, D5 or D7 and paths A, B, C with dial 3, 5, 7 only separately. The later cycles do not test the forget button: a scratch run without pb4 still selects D3. Not asserted (not printed): dial motion and where the dial rests during and after 'exploring'; any lamp or relay state; that the second push explores before it selects; 'without exploring' (no dial observable distinguishes it: the wiper passes 2-4 either way); the effect of removing the 6E wire and of the forget button (pb4), whose printed outcome ('the exploring stage again') has no observable. Hold lengths (pb6 3 s while exploring, 300 ms pushes) are script choices. Rotary run rate, coast and geometry are profile fallbacks O-R1, O-R3, O-R5; until windows are sized for a run rate as slow as 25 rpm.
